newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: FBD says 1996 growth is being maintained.
newsitem.headline: FBD says 1996 growth is being maintained.

text.p: Irish-based insurance and property group FBD Holdings Plc said on Tuesday that the organic growth achieved by the group in 1996 is being maintained in the current year.
FBD, which announced a 5.1 percent rise in pre-tax profits to 14.7 million Irish pounds last year, said that the business climate for its core activities was improving.
It said insurers who were operating at uneconomic premium levels had indicated that they were increasing their rates.
"FBD will continue to adopt a prudent approach based on solid underwriting principles to grow market share when price-driven competitive pressures ease," the company said in a statement.
FBD said prospects for the group's other financial services and property and hotel businesses in the year ahead were positive.
The company said opportunities to enhance returns to shareholders via acquisition, merger or alliance were also being sought.
"All opportunities identified will be pursued," FBD said.
FBD said turnover for 1996 had increased by 6.4 percent to 145 million Irish pounds while total assets had risen to 478.2 million punts from 450.1 million punts over the same period in 1995.
It said the 1996 performance had been achieved against the adverse market conditions that had prevailed in the insurance sector in recent years.
FBD said intense price competition in the marketplace combined with the increasing incidence and cost of motor and liability claims had been a feature of the insurance industry for some time.
"The stronger profits derive from an improvement in the insurance technical result and better returns from investments," it said.
FBD said the technical account showed that a surplus of 7.83 million Irish pounds was earned in the insurance business compared with 7.58 million punts in the previous year.
Investment income/realised gains grew by 8.4 percent to 22.76 million Irish pounds compared with 20.99 million punts previously.
It said gross written premiums in the company had grown by 4.4 percent to 106 million Irish pounds with growth coming from FBD's core rural markets as well as from the urban and commercial sector.
Net earned premiums increased by 15.8 percent to 79.37 million punts as a result of a reduction in the level of premiums ceded to re-insurers.

"This approach was taken as a prudent and economic way to grow business rather than pursuing growth solely through new business sales in a market where many business lines were underpriced," FBD said.
FBD said total net earned premiums had increased by 4.6 percent to 91.26 million punts while the net underwriting loss was 8.2 million punts.
It said a deterioration in the motor account was offset by an improved return on the property account.
FBD said income from other financial services activities and Irish and Spanish property/hotel interests had amounted to 3.2 million punts from 3.6 million punts previously.
